entries.name: Black
entries.look: The fourth of the Colour Division, who turns into a shadow when he introduces himself and who was the one who actually made the identification: nobody else in the manor is wearing a wolf-pelt onesie. He is polite, he is correct, and he is the reason the party's night stopped being about plants. Four operatives came through the door of a room the house guard had locked, and they introduced themselves in sequence, by colour, with a flourish each. *I'm Red. I'm Green. entries.name: Daniel
entries.look: Daniel is the command official who confronted the Gamma Agent after the unauthorized embassy interrogation. He began with discipline, then shifted to intelligence triage when the agent argued that the civilian operative's knowledge of the Deadman's Stamp indicated a leak. Daniel strode into the interrogation room, his heavy boots echoing ominously against the sterile tile floor. Behind him trailed two armed guards, weapons trained firmly on Wario and Waluigi's prone forms. The air crackled with tension as he approached, his crimson eyes boring into them like drills. entries.name: Darno Spriggon
entries.look: Darno Spriggon appeared during the greenhouse survey, showed Hargram's team a keychain bearing an iron ring with Iron Legion military insignia, claimed to have personally dealt with the remaining rust monsters, handed Hargram an unsent letter from Archie to Dan, said 'Let's all head inside—Archie needs this back,' and then his torch went out and everything went dark. He possessed a Legion rank ring without apparent military bearing. He knew about Archie. He had Archie's personal correspondence. entries.name: General Ironhand
entries.look: General Ironhand is the commander of the Iron Legion and the person responsible for Order 120—the execution of all Toad prisoners in Legion custody. He is not a ranting warlord or a cackling villain. He is an administrator who happens to have the authority to sign orders for mass murder, and that makes him more terrifying than any dragon. Waluigi would like General Ironhand to go sit on a Thwomp. Waluigi would like this noted for the record. Waluigi has called many people villains in this encyclopedia. Waluigi has called HIMSELF a villain, usually as a joke, sometimes as branding. General Iron

entries.name: Jack (Jackson) Melvus Miser
entries.look: Jack Melvus Miser is the eldest of the five Miser children and the reason the rest of them eat well. A paladin of the Oath of Glory who joined the Regal Lion at fifteen, he ground his way up from squire to the order's second-in-command on bandit cordons, unpriceable monster contracts, and one daylight kill on a rampaging Fire Elemental Myrmidon in front of a whole market town. entries.name: Jamesly
entries.look: Jamesly is a senior Gamma operative who entered the embassy debriefing room after the Gamma Agent used protocol authority and guard commands to corner a civilian operative. He had been monitoring the exchange, judged the agent reckless but valuable, ordered the officer to forget the encounter, and escorted the agent to a higher briefing before Command could formalize the damage. Jamesly cuts an imposing figure even in the mundane setting of a debriefing room, his tailored uniform bearing subtle insignia that mark him as one of the upper echelons of Gamma's command structure. entries.name: Koffin-K
entries.look: Koffin-K is a lonely, theatrical would-be supervillain whose fake notebook, real maps, real minions, and brief Snowdin hero status make him far more structurally important than he appears. Koffin-K exists as a fascinating paradox within the Underground's social fabric - part tragic figure, part misguided child prodigy of malice. His aspirations to conquer evil often overshadow his profound loneliness, leading him down dangerous paths in search of validation. entries.name: Legionary Agent (Gamma Division)
entries.look: The Gamma Agent is a lone legionary sent on a mission that history says is impossible. Belonging to the Gamma Expeditionary Force—a division that was supposedly wiped out 87 years ago—the agent arrived at Mount Ebott with a protocol book in one hand and a dispatch from a dead commissar in the other. Rigidly adhering to 'PROTOCOLS OF THE IRON LEGION VOLUME 1,' the agent navigated the descent into Snowdin through a mixture of luck, clumsiness, and by dragging Dracule Mihawk along for the ride. entries.name: Toadburt
entries.look: Toadburt's story is a masterclass in trading one cage for another. The Iron Legion strapped an entropy ring on him and sent him into the Feywild as a coerced operative. Now the ring is off, but Toadburt isn't free—he's working for the Shadow Estate's Archivist in exchange for gradual healing, recovering from his injuries over two-week intervals while organizing books in a vampire library. Waluigi recognizes this pattern: someone too damaged to refuse help, accepting terms from whoever offers it, trading independence for survival. It's not slavery. It's not freedom.
